findings.title: Removing `sequence_number` from hashed columns breaks tamper-evidence for entry ordering metadata
findings.evidence: `"entry_id", "session_id", "sequence_number" removed ... sequence_number ordering is enforced by previous_hash which IS hashed.`
findings.problem: `previous_hash` proves link order, not the integrity of the current row's own `sequence_number`. A row can be renumbered, duplicated, or gaps introduced without changing `record_hash` unless chain validation separately enforces contiguous numbering. That validation is not stated here.
findings.why_it_matters: The document presents the DHF as an append-only hash-chain audit foundation. If `sequence_number` is mutable outside the hash, ordering metadata can be altered without invalidating the chain, which undermines replay, audit assertions, and any consumer that orders by `sequence_number`.
findings.proposed_fix: Either keep `sequence_number` in `DhfHashColumns`, or explicitly define `ValidateChainAsync` as rejecting any non-contiguous, non-unique sequence numbering and add that requirement to ACC-02 and ACC-12.

findings.title: Cross-workstation conflict enforcement relies on an explicitly untrusted client field
findings.location: Deployment v1 → v2 Migration §6 AddinSessionId and Workstation Trust; SPEC-04 Changes §6.1 OpenOrResumeSessionCore
findings.evidence: Deployment doc: `workstation_id: client-supplied string, not a trust boundary.` SPEC-04 change: `WHERE ... addin_session_id = @AddinSessionId ... AND workstation_id != @WorkstationId` followed by `throw new CrossWorkstationSessionConflictException(...)`.
findings.problem: The hard-error collision rule depends on `workstation_id`, but the same document says that value is accepted at face value and is not trustworthy. A client can spoof another workstation name to bypass the conflict check or cause false conflicts.
findings.why_it_matters: This makes ACC-19 and the cross-workstation safety invariant non-authoritative. The system is treating an advisory field as an enforcement input.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not use `workstation_id` as a hard-enforcement discriminator until it is bound to a server-trusted identity. For v1, either introduce a server-issued/persisted workstation token or downgrade the cross-workstation check to observability-only and remove the hard-error guarantee from the contract.

findings.title: Permanent-failure path discards the only evidence needed for the mandated post-timeout recovery record
findings.location: SPEC-02 Changes §9.1.1 step 7; SPEC-00 §2 Seam B; SPEC-00 §6 Glossary `Quarantine`
findings.evidence: SPEC-02: `The stuck COM call continues running on the UI thread; it may eventually return (at which point the return is logged and discarded).` SPEC-00 Seam B: `Recovery outcome — including whether a post-timeout COM completion was detected ... — is recorded as a DHF recovery event`. Glossary `Quarantine`: late evidence `is referenced by the subsequent mandatory recovery event`.
findings.problem: In the exact stuck-call scenario, the late completion is explicitly discarded after the add-in has entered `PermanentlyFailed`. The orchestration contract still requires the later recovery event to state whether post-timeout completion was detected and to preserve continuity to the evidence, but no mechanism is defined to carry that evidence across restart/reconnect.
findings.why_it_matters: The recovery/audit contract is not implementable for the scenario this section is defining. The system loses the only direct signal of whether the timed-out COM call eventually mutated the model.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a durable handoff for permanent-failure metadata: persist the timed-out `CallId`, tool name, and any eventual late completion status locally, and require the add-in to transmit that payload on next startup so SPEC-03 can append the mandated recovery event with evidence linkage.

findings.title: Reconnect semantics after `heartbeat_timeout` with the same `AddinSessionId` are undefined
findings.evidence: `AddinSessionId changes if and only if the add-in is reloaded` and `DHF Session ... Opens on first AddinReadyMessage for a given AddinSessionId. Closes on ... heartbeat_timeout` and `DHF sessions are NOT closed on transient transport loss ... pending reconnect or heartbeat_timeout threshold.`
findings.problem: The contract does not state what happens when transport loss exceeds the heartbeat timeout but the add-in process is still running and reconnects with the same `AddinSessionId`. It is unclear whether SPEC-04 must resume, reject, or open a new session with the same epoch, and how `StateVersion` and conflict checks behave in that case.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a normal failure mode for an internet WebSocket. If SPEC-03, SPEC-04, and the add-in infer different behavior, reconnects will produce inconsistent session state, duplicate sessions, or false conflicts.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit rule for same-`AddinSessionId` reconnect after `heartbeat_timeout`: define whether it opens a new DHF session, is rejected until add-in restart, or reuses the prior session identity; define the required `StateVersion` behavior; add an acceptance test for this path.

top_3_must_fix: Restore or equivalently validate `sequence_number` integrity in the DHF hash-chain contract.
Remove hard enforcement based on untrusted `workstation_id` or make workstation identity server-trustworthy.
Define how permanent-failure late completions are durably handed off so mandatory recovery events can be recorded correctly.
